comments.text:
-el salario de 1,130 soles es referencial, nadie puede ganar menos que esa cantidad; en la práctica se gana mucho mas dependiendo del trabajo.
-el trabajo informal es transitorio, el peruano, por su constancia, con el paso de los años se FORMALIZA, forma empresas personal y familiar, pequeñas, medianas y grandes empresas a nivel nacional; asi tenemos emporios comerciales como "Gamarra", grandes mercados mayoristas de fruta, productos del mar, grandes mercados populosos Unicachi, Huamantanga y miles mas en barrios populosos y muchos que se replican en todo el pais.
-la pobreza extrema esta focaliza mayormente en los suburbios de las grandes ciudades como Lima, por la migración del campo a la ciudad. En el interior del pais, la gente tiene su parcela de tierra donde siembra y cria animales para su subsistencia.
-en Perú, como en todo pais hay pobreza, de esta condición no se salvan ni los paises de llamado "primer mundo".
-Perú no es un pais perfecto, tiene sus problemas, pero nadie se muere de hambre, los alimentos naturales, de primera calidad, son abundantes y estan al alcance de la mayoria, porque son BARATOS.
-el estado otorga educación gratuita en primaria, secundaria y universidad;  salud y medicamentos gratuitos para tods la población, a traves del SIS (Sistema Integral de salud).

comments.author: @CarlosPerezLopez-u2m
comments.text: Great video. The minimum wage is only a reference . Most Peruvians do not earn that amount. The real earned money is average 1.5 to 2x for the lower income.  The people living in the cerros ( arid hills)  is a self inflicting pain. Most of them prefer coming to Lima and suffer the pain of living this way. Actually , living in the regions (provincias) offers more opportunities to grow economically but 'the living in Lima' thing is like the 'american dream' for migrants. Peruvians pursuing the 'Lima dream' created  all those unnecesary pockets of poverty. Peruvians are resilient and hardworker people but the Lima dream is a sort of mirage. It's a fake illusion ,and it's hard to convince them otherwise. The preset minset only generates  chaos and poverty.

comments.text: Peru isn't cheap, your dollars are just strong. Once you earn local soles, every single trip to the supermarket becomes a math puzzle.

replies.author: @boink800
replies.text: In the US, our dollars are worth nothing. But in Perú our dollars actually have some value. Though, it's not nice to say it's "cheap".

replies.author: @RealLifeExplorerUS
replies.text: A place can look affordable when prices are converted into dollars, but the experience is completely different when your income is also in soles. For many local families, even ordinary grocery shopping requires careful planning and constant trade-offs.

comments.author: @Reallifeinsights.tv26
comments.text: With a monthly income of 1,130 soles in Lima, rent alone in a decent neighborhood consumes 80% of that salary.

replies.author: @RealLifeExplorerUS
replies.text: That’s a very important point. In Lima, housing can take up a huge share of a low monthly income, especially in safer or more central neighborhoods. That’s one reason many families share housing, live farther from the center, or depend on several sources of income.
